summary: Nobuhiro Ota is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo from ~1988 to 2001, he held research posts there before becoming an assistant (2002), associate professor (2007), and professor (2021) at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Nobukatsu Komai works in Buddhist studies. He studied as a research student at Taisho University and was attested in 2014 as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin.
Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from ~1955 to ~1959 and was attested as an assistant professor there in 1972.

Tensho Miyazaki specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2010), he held posts at Toyo University (~2010–2013) and the University of Tokyo (~2013–2016).

Nobumi Iyanaga specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969) and later held positions at the University of Tokyo (~2003–2004) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2008–2014).
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was attested as a researcher in 1995.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe focuses on Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Osaka University and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, he held faculty posts at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University, where he became a professor in 2015.

Nobuyuki Kaji is a philosopher and Sinologist educated at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He served on faculties including Koyasan University, Nagoya University, Osaka University (professor, 1984–1998), Koshien Junior College (president, 1998–1999), and Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

Nobuyuki Watase specializes in Indology and philosophy. After completing a master's degree at Kyoto University in ~1966, he served as an associate professor at Tokai University (~1982–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).
Nobuyuki Yamagiwa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1959–1968) under Genjun Sasaki and Issai Funahashi, and subsequently served at Otani University as an assistant, lecturer, and departmental appointee between ~1970 and ~2006.

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. She studied at Newnham College (~1911–1914) and later held academic posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines, he held major faculty posts at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi, and served as professor at Komazawa University from 1985 to 2011.

Noriaki Hosoda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as an assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University, and was attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Noriaki Inoue specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University from ~1949 to ~1953 and later served there as a professor from ~1980 to ~1999.

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He served as a lecturer, associate professor, and professor at Bukkyo University from 1976 until becoming professor emeritus in 2015.
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He was attested as an assistant at Osaka University of Foreign Studies in 1962.
Norihiro Matsuura specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. In 2026, he is attested as a faculty member at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Norihisa Baba is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He joined the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, becoming a professor in 2019.
